actions.action: Slide plant out of pot and check roots (including for mushy roots or sour smell)
Trim any brown, mushy or smelly roots
Repot into a pot 1-2 inches wider with fresh well-draining mix plus perlite
Water thoroughly after repotting until it drains
Prune long bare vines back hard just above a node
Remove fully yellow or dead leaves
Plant rooted cuttings back in the pot to fill it out
Move plant to bright, indirect light
Check soil and water when top 1-2 inches are dry
Fertilize lightly in spring and summer

reason: The answer identifies the leggy, overgrown, root-bound plant and recommends a hard prune, repotting and propagation, which matches the confirmed fix, and nothing in it is harmful.
